reasoning:
I'm going back through the conflicting hypotheses across rounds—no clean geometric rule held up consistently, increasing-x fit most but not all episodes, and now I'm weighing whether color priority or increasing-y within color might explain the remaining exceptions better than what's been tried so far.

Within same colour, the tie-break evidence is genuinely conflicted — round 3's y-ascending rule and round 2's x-ascending rule give different answers for the same pair of red cubes, and round 1's near-then-far ordering contradicts both. I'll settle on committing to blue-first colour priority since that's consistent across rounds, but acknowledge the same-colour ordering isn't reliably predictable from the data I have.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: point at the cube sitting on a highlighted area that has the smallest x (the robot's right-most highlighted cube), using its current position.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: point at the first entry of the pending_cubes list as written at this step under the memory instruction (blue before red before green; among same-coloured cubes the smallest x), using that cube's current position, or the highlighted-area position from the execution step when the cube is not listed in the scene.

edits.modify_from: and order the entries by increasing x, i.e. the robot's right-most cube first and the left-most cube last, regardless of the order the areas are printed in. e.g. [[107, 97], [116, 135], [80, 145]].
edits.modify_to: and order the entries by colour first: blue cubes first, then red, then green, then any other colour; among cubes of the same colour, order by increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, the left-most last). The order the areas are printed in plays no part. e.g. [[106, 104], [53, 101]] (blue at [106, 104] before green at [53, 101]); two red cubes at [81, 125] and [113, 120] -> [[113, 120], [81, 125]].

edits.modify_from: In nearly every episode that sequence is increasing x (the robot's right-most cube first, the left-most last); when the episode's pick order and increasing-x order agree, the list is simply the cubes sorted by increasing x.
edits.modify_to: The order is read from the episode, not computed from the scene: no coordinate sort reproduces it in every episode. In the episodes seen so far a blue highlighted cube is picked before a highlighted cube of any other colour; among cubes of the same colour the order varies.

revision.refused: The report's tie-break of increasing y within a colour stays out: round 1 recorded one episode picking the far cube first and another picking near, then far, then middle, so a y sort is contradicted by earlier rounds, and round 2's multi-cube episodes agreed with increasing x; the same-colour tie-break therefore keeps increasing x rather than swapping one coordinate rule for another that fails elsewhere. What is committed is the colour priority, blue first, which round 1 (blue picked before red) and round 3 (blue before green) both show and no round contradicts, and the removal of the annotator prompt's false claim that the order is nearly always increasing x. The annotation keeps the true pick order, as in rounds 1 and 2; the button-press step remains the one step where the policy must guess, and the ordering is now stated once, in the memory instruction, with rule 3 pointing at the first entry of the list written there.
